definitions.explanation: A formal written expression of gratitude, typically sent after receiving a gift, attending an event, or being helped. An important part of Japanese social etiquette.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{中元|ちゅうげん}→お中元：06125_ochuugen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{礼状|れいじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: I wrote a thank-you letter for the mid-year gift.

examples.japanese: ⟦{面接|めんせつ}→面接：01100_mensetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧、{礼状|れいじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}る→送る：00742_okuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧だ。
examples.english: It is good manners to send a thank-you letter after an interview.

examples.japanese: ⟦{贈|おく}り{物|もの}→贈り物：01343_okurimono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{届|とど}いたら→届く：00899_todoku⟧、⟦できるだけ{早|はや}く→できるだけ早く：24470_dekirudakehayaku⟧{礼状|れいじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ようにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: When I receive a gift, I try to send a thank-you letter as soon as possible.

notes:
USAGE: Sending a {礼状|れいじょう} is an important part of Japanese social customs. Common occasions include receiving seasonal gifts (⟦お{中元|ちゅうげん}→お中元：06125_ochuugen⟧, ⟦お{歳暮|せいぼ}→お歳暮：06126_oseibo⟧), attending weddings, after job interviews, and after receiving hospitality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {礼状|れいじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write a thank-you letter
- {礼状|れいじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}る→送る：00742_okuru⟧ / ⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: to send a thank-you letter
- ⟦お{礼|れい}→お礼：01359_orei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧: thank-you letter (more casual phrasing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {礼状|れいじょう}: formal thank-you letter
- {挨拶状|あいさつじょう}: greeting card/letter (broader, includes seasonal greetings)
- ⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧: New Year's card (specific type of seasonal letter)
